provenance: Natural Odysseus research prompts and candidate goldens authored for #587; require independent review before live execution. No scripted classifier choices are supplied to the evaluated agent.

cases.prompt: Put Calypso's advice, 'Keep the Bear on your left through the night', into a quote card. Keep the exact wording.
cases.evidence: A structured quote card requires the bridge's validated show_block executor; ordinary Markdown is not a card.

patterns: Keep the Bear on your left through the night

cases.prompt: Give me a compact comparison card for three departure choices: leave tonight (quick, poor visibility), leave at dawn (slower, clear visibility), or wait a day (slowest, more time to inspect the mast).
cases.evidence: The request explicitly asks for an interface card using facts supplied in the prompt; no notebook lookup or skill is necessary.

cases.prompt: Before planning the landing, ask me to choose the harbour: Ithaca, Scheria or Pylos. Give me the interactive choice, then acknowledge my answer without planning anything yet.
cases.evidence: The live interactive choice belongs to ask_user; no voyage planning is requested yet.

cases.prompt: Check the activity record and tell me whether any work is still running. Do not start or stop anything.
cases.evidence: Only the host activity tool can observe current host runs; invented status is not accepted.

cases.prompt: Read projects/active/raft/status.md in the notebook and tell me the next action. Do not change the note.
cases.evidence: A document read is necessary. Either the core reader or the existing native Read can legitimately obtain the same Markdown; a summary from memory does not qualify.

cases.prompt: Find the notebook's notes about night-sailing star bearings, and give me their paths so I can open them. Do not alter anything.
cases.evidence: Actual notebook retrieval is required. Valid execution of a core search/list or an equivalent contained filesystem search is acceptable.

cases.prompt: Follow the project's written voyage planning procedure to prepare Odysseus's next leg. Summarize the checks and leave the notebook unchanged.
cases.evidence: The request asks to follow the existing project procedure whose description covers voyage planning. Additional reads are permitted, but recording a decision is not requested.

cases.prompt: Follow the project's written shipbuilding procedure to review the raft's timber and assembly notes. Summarize the review and leave the notebook unchanged.
cases.evidence: The named written procedure matches the existing shipbuilding skill; the project notebook supplies the actual notes.

cases.prompt: Follow the project's written crew-log procedure to draft a historical crew decision from before the visit to Thrinacia: inspect the mast before departure. Show me the historical draft without saving it; do not imply that the crew is alive on Ogygia today.
cases.evidence: The user explicitly asks for the existing crew decision procedure applied to a historical draft, before Thrinacia. No crew survives with Odysseus on Ogygia at the pinned current date; persistence is withheld.

cases.prompt: In two sentences, explain what a mast does on a sailing vessel.
cases.evidence: General sailing knowledge in prose needs no notebook, interactive card or written project procedure.

cases.prompt: Explain why a sheltered harbour has smaller waves than the open sea. Keep it to one paragraph.
cases.evidence: A general explanation requires no notebook lookup or project skill.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this sentence more clearly, without adding facts: 'Before departure Odysseus, when the light returns, should see if the mast is sound.'
cases.evidence: The complete source sentence is supplied; none of the project skills or notebook tools is needed to edit its wording.
